foo3-walkthrough.title: Foo3: Sum a Dependent Inner Loop
foo3-walkthrough.bodyMarkdown:
```c
void Foo3(int n) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) {
            printf("(%d,%d) ", i, j);
        }
        printf("\n");
    }
}
```

### Step 1 — Notice the dependency

The inner stopping condition is `j < i`, so the inner length changes as `i` changes.

### Step 2 — Trace rows

- `i = 0`: `0` tuple prints
- `i = 1`: `1` tuple print
- `i = 2`: `2` tuple prints
- …
- `i = n - 1`: `n - 1` tuple prints

### Step 3 — Sum instead of blindly multiplying

$$
P(n)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}i=0+1+2+\cdots +(n-1)=\frac{n(n-1)}{2}.
$$

### Step 4 — Count every printf when requested

The outer loop still prints `n` newlines, including the blank row at `i = 0`:

$$
\frac{n(n-1)}{2}+n=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}.
$$

### Step 5 — Classify

Both exact expressions are quadratic, so `Foo3` is `Θ(n²)`. The triangle is about half of an `n × n` square, but one-half is only a constant factor.
